liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Race Is On** (1 review): Reviewer suggests streaming this song to compare the three available versions [9]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Phil's bass playing on this song is striking, with heavy bombs dropped throughout [14]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Reviewer praises the wonderfully drawn-out, inspired jamming in this version [15]
- **U.S. Blues** (1 other source): Played as the encore [1]
- Features a space-funk riff from nowhere, rivaling Parliament; some hear it as a prototype of the Shakedown lick [18]

## Setlist highlights

- **Friend Of The Devil**: back after 112 archived shows (646 days) [19]
- **PlayinÃÂ´ In The Band**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [19]
- **Phil And ned**: rare: 14 archived performances [19]
- **HeÃÂ´s Gone**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [19]
- **TruckinÃÂ´**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [19]
- **Caution Jam**: back after 356 archived shows (1663 days) [19]

## The recordings

- **gd74-09-18.sbd.miller.20732.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 26 songs; 209 min; rated 4.78/5 by 27 [1]. Said about its sound: Phil's bass is prominent from the start, while vocals are somewhat weak until the band settles in; Of three versions offered, the first has Garcia's guitar slightly lower in the mix; the third has somewhat hollow vocals; Reviewer calls the sound top-notch, only surpassable by a multitrack release [8][9][10][15]
- **gd74-09-18.sbd.bertha-ashley.21925.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 26 songs; 209 min; rated 4.77/5 by 13 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer describes the Bertha remix as crystal clear; Sound seems to lack some midrange but is not bad [16][17]
- **gd1974-09-18.sbd.miller.20675.shnf**: soundboard; 26 songs; 209 min; rated 4.75/5 by 20 [2]
- **gd1974-09-18.sbd.jeffm.3398.shnf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 178 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]

## Around the show

- Jerry sings the opening number of both sets, which the reviewer treats as a clue to the show's quality [7]
- Reviewer says long cosmic jams are better found at the 5/14 and 2/24 shows, but this one is tight and exciting [7]
- Reviewer sees Europe 74 tour as uneven due to overindulgence, yet this show finds the band clear and focused [7]
- The band builds a vibe and flows naturally rather than a patchwork of songs, which reviewer says used to happen often [10]
- In context of summer and fall 1974 concerts, reviewer finds this one stands out from the crowd [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd74-09-18.sbd.miller.20732.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Reviewer says the Bertha re-master on the archive sounds far better than this source, and suggests comparing songs from each; Soundboard to reel-to-master, to DAT, Sonic Solutions, CD, EAC, then SHN by Charlie Miller; Source was pre-FM GDH production discs, transferred as three audio discs, two SHN discs [1][11]
- **gd74-09-18.sbd.bertha-ashley.21925.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]
- **gd1974-09-18.sbd.miller.20675.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Rm -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD -> EAC -> SHN [2]
- **gd1974-09-18.sbd.jeffm.3398.shnf**: transferred by DAE(EAC) and SHN Encoding By Jeff M.; source: SBD>MR>?>DAT>CDR>EAC>SHN [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by @donelichterman: [Don’s Pick This Week is from the Parc des Expositions on 09-19-1974 - The Grateful Dead Live](https://thegratefuldeadlive.com/dons-pick-this-week-uis-from-the-parc-des-expositions-on-09-19-1974/) [20]
